name: sv_breakpoint
headline_stat: split-read recall and breakpoint-position accuracy vs. breakpoint density

construction.description: Take a clean 50 Mb slice of human chr1. Implant dense structural variation — inversions, translocations, and tandem expansions at ~1-5 kb spacing — so a large fraction of reads span a breakpoint. Record every breakpoint in a truth BED.
construction.command: VISOR HACk -g ../../../homo_sapiens/chr1/data/reference/reference.fasta -b svs.bed -o visor_out && mv visor_out/h1.fa reference.fasta
construction.notes: Generate svs.bed with VISOR format SVs at the desired spacing before running HACk. See VISOR documentation for BED format. SURVIVOR can also be used to generate the SV BED.

simulation.command: dwgsim -1 150 -2 150 -C 30 -z {rng_seed} ../reference/reference.fasta reads && mv reads.bwa.read1.fastq.gz reads_1.fastq.gz && mv reads.bwa.read2.fastq.gz reads_2.fastq.gz
simulation.notes: At 150bp reads and 1kb SV spacing, roughly 30% of reads will span a breakpoint — sufficient for split-read analysis.

sweep.notes: Build three versions of the synthetic reference at each spacing. Denser spacing means more reads spanning breakpoints and harder disambiguation.

truth.eval_notes: At each breakpoint: did the aligner split-map correctly, soft-clip, or mismap? Report split-read recall and breakpoint-position accuracy (within 5 bp) vs. density. Distinguish by SV type.
